title: 长对话主旨题
goal: 概括贯穿对话的中心事项；识别交谈需要解决的问题。

points.label: 概括贯穿对话的中心事项
识别交谈需要解决的问题

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲（2016年修订版）
sources.used: 依据课程课表选择长对话语言训练范围；材料与题目为原创。

body.p: 主要话题题问双方一直在谈的事。交谈目的题问这次谈话要解决什么问题。题干有 mainly 或 purpose 时，答案要概括整段对话，不能只取一个细节。

body.box:
What are the speakers mainly discussing?
Why does the speaker ask to meet?
What problem are they trying to resolve?

body.p: 例如，双方商量社区画室的使用时段：话题是使用安排，目的是解决两个活动时间冲突。开头提到参加过画展，只是背景。

steps.d: 分清问的是话题还是目的。mainly discussing 问谈的是什么，trying to resolve 问要解决的问题。
把开头提出的事和后面反复谈的事对照。先说 storage，后面比较柜子、标签和借还流程，中心仍是物品存放。
看选项能否覆盖主要的几轮对话。只谈柜子的颜色太窄，谈所有社区服务太宽。
用结尾的方案核对对话要解决的问题。Let's label the boxes 解决的是拿错东西，推不出要买新设备。

cards.title: 中心与交谈目的
rows: 看反复谈到的对象，不只看第一个名词。
We met at the market. Can we discuss the shared freezer? → Freezer use.
写成要做的事和要解决的问题。
Food keeps being left unmarked. Can we agree on labels? → Establish a labeling arrangement.
几个方案针对的是同一个问题。
More shelves or fewer stored boxes? → Improving storage.
用结尾的决定核对中心。
Let's trial smaller boxes. → Testing a response to limited space.

cards.title: 概括范围的辨析
rows: We need a quieter practice space. Thick curtains might help; moving rooms is another option.
The newsletter arrives late. We discuss editing, printing, and collection.
After the street festival, we met to decide how to store borrowed tables.
The pool reopened last month. Today we need to resolve overlapping club bookings.
We discuss access to one community kitchen on weekends.
We compare two ways to label donated coats.

body.box:
A: The ceramics fair went well, but I'd like to discuss how we return the borrowed display stands. Some owners can collect them, while others need delivery.
B: Let's group the stands by owner first. Then we can agree on collection times and arrange transport for the rest.
A: That would prevent mixing up the returns.

Why is the discussion taking place?
1. To evaluate sales at the fair.
2. To select new display stands.
3. To coordinate the return of borrowed equipment.
4. To introduce transport for every future event.

body.p: 依据是 I'd like to discuss how we return the borrowed display stands。后面谈的 collect、delivery、group by owner 都是归还的安排，即第三项。fair 只是背景。transport 是这次归还的一个环节，与以后的活动无关。

cards.title: 干扰项
rows: 只是归还方式中的一项。
开头提到，双方没有接着谈。
Organizing transport for all future events
对话只谈这一次的归还。
Buying stands to avoid future returns
对话没有谈到购买展架。

lines.text: The bakery's notice board is crowded with old advertisements. Could we agree on a way to keep it useful? Customers can't easily find current local events.
We could date each notice and remove it after the event. A separate section for ongoing services would keep those notices from being removed by mistake.

items.stem: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
options: Advertising a new bakery to local customers.
Keeping a public notice board current.
Removing all advertisements for ongoing services.
Selecting dates for the next local events.
items.why: 依据是 Could we agree on a way to keep it useful? 后面谈的给通知标日期、活动过后撤下，都是让公告栏保持最新，即第二项。

lines.text: Our neighborhood film club has gained new members, and some can't see the subtitles from the back. I'd like to discuss the seating before we choose another film.
We could leave wider gaps between rows or put the screen higher. Let's compare those options in the hall before changing our film selection.

items.stem: Why does the first speaker start the conversation?
options: To replace subtitled films with other selections.
To welcome the new members to the film club.
To choose the next film before changing seats.
To improve members' view of the subtitles.
items.why: 依据是 some can't see the subtitles from the back 和 I'd like to discuss the seating。谈座位和屏幕高度，是为了让会员看清字幕，即第四项。

lines.text: The craft market used to be held in the school gym. Since moving outdoors, we've had difficulty keeping the queue clear of the stalls.
Perhaps we could mark a route and move the payment desk. Both changes would let people browse without blocking those waiting to pay.

items.stem: Which topic covers the main exchange?
options: Managing customer movement at the outdoor market.
Returning the craft market to the school gym.
Selecting new products for the market stalls.
Comparing the gym and the outdoor site for stalls.
items.why: 依据是 keeping the queue clear of the stalls 和 mark a route。双方谈的是露天市场的人流，school gym 只是以前的地点，即第一项。

lines.text: The local choir has kept recordings of its concerts for years, but the files have inconsistent names. Can we decide on a naming system before adding this year's recordings?
Let's include the date, venue, and song title. That should make it easier to locate a performance without opening every file.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To decide which venue will host the next concert.
To select the songs for this year's performance.
To make stored concert recordings easier to identify.
To replace all recordings from earlier years.
items.why: 依据是 Can we decide on a naming system 和 easier to locate a performance。统一文件命名，是为了方便查找录音，即第三项。

lines.text: Our community has collected oral memories about the old railway station, but visitors rarely listen beyond the first minute. I'd like to discuss the way the recordings are presented.
We could divide them into shorter extracts about journeys, station jobs, and farewells. That would let visitors choose a subject instead of starting a long recording without knowing its focus.
Good. We should keep the speakers' context in short introductions. I want easier access to the stories, not a new account of railway engineering.

options: Explaining the engineering of the former railway.
Collecting more memories about station jobs.
Writing longer introductions for each speaker.
Presenting recorded memories in a more accessible form.
items.why: 依据是 I'd like to discuss the way the recordings are presented，以及后面的 shorter extracts 和 short introductions。双方谈的是回忆录音怎样呈现，即第四项。

items.stem: What need motivates the proposed change?
options: Correcting the speakers' descriptions of engineering.
Helping visitors engage with the collected stories.
Shortening the collection by removing farewells.
Adding more detail on railway engineering.
items.why: 依据是 visitors rarely listen beyond the first minute 和 I want easier access to the stories。改动是为了让听众更容易听进这些故事，即第二项。

lines.text: Clara, can we talk about the way our neighborhood food cooperative distributes its weekly boxes? Membership has grown, but several members say they receive vegetables they can't use. I'd like us to consider a more flexible system before the next growing season.

I've heard that too, Jonas. Some households cook every evening, while others only prepare meals at home on weekends. The standard box suits the first group better. Changing the size alone wouldn't solve the problem if the contents remained unsuitable.

What about allowing everyone to choose individual vegetables? We already publish a list of what the growers expect to provide. Members could select from that list, and we'd assemble boxes according to their requests instead of using the same combination for everyone.

That would offer choice, but the volunteers would spend much longer packing. The growers' lists also change when a crop isn't ready. We'd need to contact members again whenever a requested item became unavailable, which could create considerable extra work.

Then perhaps we could keep the standard box and add an exchange table at collection time. Members who don't want an item could leave it there and choose something another household has offered. We wouldn't need to repack every box.

That seems practical, provided the exchanges happen during the staffed collection period. We shouldn't leave fresh produce outside overnight. The table could go beside the entrance, where a volunteer could explain the arrangement without blocking people collecting their boxes.

Let's try that for a month and ask members whether it reduces unwanted produce. I'll draft a short notice explaining that exchanges depend on what's available; nobody would be promised a particular replacement.
Agreed. I'll discuss the table with the collection team. We can reconsider individual selection later if this simpler change doesn't meet members' needs.

items.stem: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Letting members choose every vegetable themselves.
Comparing the crops available in different growing seasons.
Making produce distribution better suit members' needs.
Changing the size of the standard weekly box.
items.why: 依据是开头的 several members say they receive vegetables they can't use。后面的自选和交换方案都针对这个问题，即第三项。

items.stem: Why does Jonas initiate the discussion?
options: To find a workable response to unwanted box contents.
To persuade members to cook at home every evening.
To obtain a fixed crop list for the next season.
To reduce the time volunteers spend packing boxes.
items.why: 依据是 several members say they receive vegetables they can't use 和 I'd like us to consider a more flexible system。Jonas 想解决箱里的菜用不上的问题，即第一项。

items.stem: Which title best covers both the problem and the proposed solution?
options: Recruiting More Volunteers to Pack Individual Vegetable Orders
Protecting Every Crop by Moving the Collection Table Indoors
Replacing the Standard Box With Individual Vegetable Choices
Reducing Unwanted Produce Through a Collection-Time Exchange
items.why: 依据是 add an exchange table at collection time 和 ask members whether it reduces unwanted produce。问题是用不上的菜，办法是领取时交换，即第四项。

lines.text: Thanks for meeting me, Dev. I'm preparing a display about the old riverside laundry, and I need help deciding how to present the workers' accounts. We have photographs of the building, but I don't want the exhibition to become just a history of its machinery.

That makes sense, Lena. The interviews describe how shifts were organized, how people learned the work, and how they supported new employees. Those subjects tell visitors something the photographs alone can't show. Have you considered arranging the display around a typical working day?

I have, though the accounts come from different decades. If we combine everything into one day, visitors might assume that all the workers were there together. I want a clear structure without hiding changes in the way the laundry was run.

Then perhaps use themes, with a date attached to each account. One section could cover learning a task, another the pace of work, and another relationships between colleagues. That would let visitors compare experiences while seeing when each person worked there.

I like that approach. There are also two accounts that disagree about breaks. One worker remembers informal pauses, while another describes a strict bell. Should we leave one out to avoid confusing people?

I'd keep both and include the dates and departments. Different rules may have applied in different places or periods. We shouldn't settle the disagreement unless the records support a clear explanation. The contrast can show that experiences weren't identical.

Then I'll organize the accounts by theme and make their context visible. The machinery photographs can support the stories instead of determining the whole layout. Could you check whether my captions preserve the speakers' meanings?
Certainly. Send me the draft with the original extracts. I'll compare them and flag any wording that makes an individual memory sound like a rule that applied to everyone.

items.stem: What is the central subject of the conversation?
options: Reconstructing the laundry's original mechanical equipment.
Organizing workers' memories for a historical display.
Resolving every disagreement about the laundry's break rules.
Combining several decades into one typical working day.
items.why: 依据是开头的 deciding how to present the workers' accounts 和结尾的 I'll organize the accounts by theme。双方一直在谈怎样展示工人的回忆，即第二项。

items.stem: What does Lena mainly seek from Dev?
options: Permission to replace all interviews with machinery photographs.
Proof that the strict bell applied to every department.
Advice on presenting accounts clearly without distorting them.
Help choosing which account about breaks to leave out.
items.why: 依据是 I want a clear structure without hiding changes 和 check whether my captions preserve the speakers' meanings。Lena 要的是既清楚又不改变原意的展示办法，即第三项。

items.stem: Which problem are the speakers trying to solve throughout the discussion?
options: How to make varied experiences coherent while preserving context.
How to prove that all memories describe the same workplace rules.
How to settle which worker remembered the breaks correctly.
How to remove dates so visitors can follow one working day.
items.why: 依据是 use themes, with a date attached to each account 和 I'll organize the accounts by theme and make their context visible。按主题组织，同时保留日期和部门，即第一项。
